spec_refs: VCSX-SPEC.md Section 5.3 "Matching Algorithm and the `#class` Fallback"
description: Select at most one policy edge for a trigger by most-specific-wins over the fallback ladder, or fall through to the built-in default.
given: an edge set and a trigger token
expect: the `on` key of the selected edge (null when none matched), the resulting action, and any action argument the vector pins
notes: A proto class is not supplied: the implementation derives it from the Section 4.3 registry, as `proto_class(op, reason)` in Section 12.1 does.
`action` is the matched edge's `do`, or the Section 5.4 built-in default. `continue` and `no_op` are Section 5.4 outcomes, not Section 5.2 actions.
Keys absent from `expect` are unconstrained, so a vector may assert the selection without asserting an unspecified default.

vectors.description: Most-specific-wins: the exact op:reason edge is selected over both fallbacks.
An op:#class edge catches a reason of that class with no exact edge (Section 13.1).
A #class edge catches an otherwise-unmatched result (Section 13.1).
The ladder prefers op:#class over the bare #class rung.
A push:#error edge does not catch a needs_caller reason on the same operation.
An op:#class edge is scoped to its operation; a same-class reason on another operation falls through.
Built-in default for the error class (Section 5.4).
The universal `blocked` reason is class needs_caller at every gated operation, so a gate-blocked create_pr escalates by default (Sections 4.3, 5.4, 6.6).
`merge:blocked` is the `before:merge` gate block at needs_caller, so a merge:#needs_caller edge catches it (Sections 4.3, 6.6).
The universal `unsupported` reason is class error and is defined for every operation, including the read-only ones (Sections 4.3, 9.3).
Built-in default for the needs_caller class (Section 5.4).
A done result with no edge continues the flow (Section 5.4).
A done result is an ordinary trigger when the policy binds it.
The #class ladder applies to the done class as it does to the other two.
A lifecycle position is matched exactly (Section 5.3).

An edge does not declare its execution context; the artifact it was declared in fixes it (Sections 3.2, 6.5). A policy written against the declared form is still valid and the key is ignored under Section 6.1's unknown-key rule, so the edge matches and dispatches as if it carried none — the context it names is not consulted and does not affect selection (Sections 5.3, 6.1).
Class edges never catch a lifecycle position (Section 5.3, "No class fallback"), so the position is unmatched and the operation proceeds (Section 5.4).
A policy that binds only some of the required positions leaves the rest unbound; the operation proceeds (Section 5.4).

A token that is neither a known lifecycle position nor an `op:reason` / `op:#class` / `#class` form over a known operation is not a trigger; the policy is refused at validation with `unknown_trigger` rather than validating and never firing (Sections 5.1, 6.5, 6.11). Decision 0122 removed the signal trigger kind, so a policy written against it fails loudly.
